experiment: P00.4 Linux WPE Remote Web Inspector HTTP endpoint
scope: A standalone Flutter Linux/WPE probe was run with WEBKIT_INSPECTOR_HTTP_SERVER bound to loopback. The remote inspector target list contained the probe page and the server returned its Main.html frontend. This verifies endpoint and target discovery only; it does not verify an attached inspector command session or Chrome DevTools Protocol.

results.pluginSourceObservation: The pinned Linux plugin implementation defaults enableDeveloperExtras to true and calls webkit_settings_set_enable_developer_extras(); the Dart platform capability metadata still reports isInspectable unsupported.

limitations: This inspector run explicitly disabled the WPE sandbox and GBM; it is endpoint feasibility evidence, not production-security or hardware-rendering evidence.
The HTTP target list and Main.html were fetched, but no inspector UI was attached and no inspector protocol command received a verified response.
The WPE Inspector protocol is not claimed to be Chrome DevTools Protocol; the pinned Flutter Linux plugin reports CDP unsupported.
No macOS WKWebView/Safari Inspector or full product integration was tested.
The captured memory snapshots are exploratory single-run values and do not satisfy docs/04 multi-round sampling.
artifactStorageNote: inspector-ui.html is stored gzip-compressed to preserve the original 2,680-byte HTTP body; inspector-ui.headers is normalized from CRLF to LF for repository whitespace checks.
